text: The study evaluates the performance of ColBERT using the MS MARCO and TREC-CAR datasets.

The ColBERT model utilizes separate BERT architectures for query and document encoding, differentiating them by adding specific [Q] and [D] tokens to the respective inputs.

The authors propose that summing maximum similarity scores allows for efficient top-k retrieval by enabling vector-similarity algorithms to skip documents without computing the full interaction matrix.

The ColBERT model utilizes a late-interaction mechanism where a query encoder and a document encoder process inputs into sets of context-dependent embeddings.
The ColBERT model utilizes a late-interaction mechanism where a query encoder and a document encoder process inputs into single, non-contextualized scalar vectors.
The proposed indexing method utilizes multiple GPUs to process document batches in parallel, thereby improving the throughput of the offline encoding process.
The proposed indexing method relies on a single CPU to process document batches sequentially, thereby reducing the throughput of the offline encoding process.
The study evaluates full retrieval performance by having models retrieve the top 1,000 documents from a collection of 8.8 million MS MARCO documents for each query.
The study evaluates full retrieval performance by having models retrieve the top 100 documents from a collection of 880,000 MS MARCO documents for each query.

The authors suggest that CLIP models, which utilize natural language supervision on large datasets, offer a distinct avenue for investigating whether observed failures are specific to ImageNet or inherent to deep learning.
The architecture of CLIP relies on a single dot product operation within a shared embedding space to facilitate interaction between image and text data.
The architecture of CLIP relies on a dense joint attention mechanism to facilitate interaction between image and text data.

The BASIC method scales batch sizes up to 16k by utilizing hundreds of chips and incorporating a large private classification dataset.
The BASIC method scales batch sizes up to 160k by utilizing hundreds of chips and incorporating a large private classification dataset.
The authors initialize the learnable bias term to -10 and the temperature parameter to the logarithm of 10 to prevent large initial optimization steps caused by class imbalance.
The authors initialize the learnable bias term to 10 and the temperature parameter to the logarithm of 10 to prevent large initial optimization steps caused by class imbalance.
The contrastive learning framework operates under the assumption that text captions from different images are unrelated to the current image, although this premise is often imperfect.
The contrastive learning framework operates under the assumption that text captions from different images are always perfectly related to the current image, and this premise is never imperfect.
The SigLiT model was trained using the LION optimizer with a peak learning rate of $1 \times 10^{-4}$ and a weight decay of $1 \times 10^{-7}$.

The SoViT model achieved a validation accuracy of 86.7% on the ImageNet-1k dataset using linear probing.
The function $f_k(x, t)$ is characterized as monotone decreasing for values of $x$ less than $\hat{x}$ and monotone increasing for values greater than $\hat{x}$.
The function $f_k(x, t)$ is characterized as monotone increasing for values of $x$ less than $\hat{x}$ and monotone decreasing for values greater than $\hat{x}$.
The study estimates the parameters of the proposed scaling law by minimizing the relative error, under the assumption that data is unlimited and non-target shape dimensions are sufficiently large.
The study estimates the parameters of the proposed scaling law by minimizing the absolute error, under the assumption that data is unlimited and non-target shape dimensions are sufficiently large.

The study restricts input documents to the initial 512 word pieces to accommodate the sequence length constraints of transformer models.
The study restricts input documents to the initial 1024 word pieces to accommodate the sequence length constraints of transformer models.
The proposed benchmark is designed to assess retrieval systems across a spectrum of domains, including both broad sources like Wikipedia and highly specialized scientific publications.
The proposed benchmark is designed to assess retrieval systems exclusively within broad, generic domains such as Wikipedia, excluding any specialized scientific fields.
Transformer-based models typically operate with a maximum sequence length of 512 word pieces, which creates a fundamental barrier when comparing them against methods designed for longer documents.
Transformer-based models typically operate with a maximum sequence length of 1024 word pieces, which creates a fundamental barrier when comparing them against methods designed for longer documents.
Late-interaction re-ranking models achieve superior out-of-distribution generalization but incur inference latencies exceeding 350 milliseconds.
Late-interaction re-ranking models achieve superior out-of-distribution generalization but incur inference latencies below 20 milliseconds.

For standard 128-dimensional vectors, the residual component in the ColBERTv2 compression scheme occupies 16 bytes when using 1-bit residuals.

The study evaluates the performance of PLAID ColBERTv2 alongside baseline systems including BM25, SPLADEv2, and DPR using test set queries.

The authors attribute the high computational cost of index lookups in vanilla ColBERTv2 to the necessity of reshaping and padding 2D tensors into 3D structures to accommodate variable passage lengths.

The secondary category clustering split is designed to assess a model's ability to distinguish between fine-grained sub-categories while ignoring the separation between distinct main categories.

The Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) encompasses 112 languages and includes only two distinct text embedding tasks.

The authors note that SimCSE exhibits strong results on clustering and retrieval tasks even though it performs poorly on semantic textual similarity.

The multilingual MiniLM model achieves the highest overall performance on multilingual classification and Semantic Textual Similarity tasks, surpassing the multilingual MPNet in most languages.

The BLIP-2 framework requires fine-tuning both the image encoder and the large language model to perform vision-language tasks, resulting in higher computational costs than prior methods.

The study utilizes a pre-training corpus of 129 million images that includes 115 million samples from the LAION400M dataset, employing the CapFilt method to select the top two captions per image based on CLIP ViT-L/14 similarity scores.

The study utilizes a prefix language modeling loss for encoder-decoder architectures, where the visual features and prefix text serve as encoder inputs while the suffix text acts as the decoder's generation target.
The study utilizes a prefix language modeling loss for encoder-decoder architectures, where the suffix text serves as the encoder input while the prefix text acts as the decoder's generation target.

The authors utilize a Q-Former module connected to a static image encoder, optimizing it with three distinct objectives that employ varying attention masking techniques to facilitate the extraction of text-relevant visual features.

The authors utilize a Q-Former module connected to a trainable image encoder, optimizing it with a single objective that employs a uniform attention masking technique to facilitate the extraction of text-relevant visual features.

The authors argue that the gathering phase of multi-vector models significantly increases computational overhead by requiring the loading of all token embeddings, not just those retrieved in the initial stage.

The authors argue that the gathering phase of multi-vector models reduces computational overhead by only requiring the loading of token embeddings that were successfully retrieved in the initial stage.
The fXTR' method differs from fColBERT by avoiding the loading of token vectors and instead reusing scores from the initial token retrieval stage.
The fXTR' method differs from fColBERT by loading all token vectors and exhaustively recomputing pairwise token similarities to determine max values.

The qualitative analysis indicates that the top-ranked token "la" retrieved by T5-ColBERT for the query "lauren london age?" was associated with a context regarding Laura Bush, which was deemed relevant.

The Gemma model family consists of two parameter sizes, specifically 2 billion and 7 billion, and is reported to surpass comparable open-source models on the majority of the 18 evaluated text-based tasks.

The proposed Token Pooling method reduces the number of indexed vectors by averaging token representations using clustering techniques, with hierarchical clustering identified as a particularly effective approach.

The authors define the pooling factor as a compression metric where a value of 2 results in a 100% reduction of the stored vector count.

The proposed Token Pooling method reduces document representation size by clustering vectors and applying mean pooling, a process that requires no additional training when applied to pre-trained ColBERT models.

The proposed Token Pooling method reduces document representation size by clustering vectors and applying mean pooling, a process that requires extensive fine-tuning when applied to pre-trained ColBERT models.
Clavié et al. propose a clustering-based token pooling method designed to significantly decrease the number of vectors required for multi-vector retrieval systems like ColBERT.
Clavié et al. propose a clustering-based token pooling method designed to significantly increase the number of vectors required for multi-vector retrieval systems like ColBERT.
